“Would you repeat, Dr Seldon, your thoughts concerning the future of Trantor?
A: I have said. and I say again, that Trantor will lie in ruins within the next five centuries.
Q: You do not consider your statement a disloyal one?
A: No, sir. Scientific truth is beyond loyalty and disloyalty.
Q: You are sure that your statement represents scientific truth?
Q: On what basis?
A: On the basis of the mathematics of psychohistory.
Q: Can you prove that this mathematics is valid?
A: Only to another mathematician.
Q: (with a smile) Your claim then, is that your truth is of so esoteric a nature that it is beyond the understanding of a plain man. It seems to me that truth should be clearer than that, less mysterious, more open to the mind.
A: It presents no difficulties to some minds. The physics of energy transfer, which we know as thermodynamics, has been clear and true through all the history of man since the mythical ages, yet there may be people present who would find it impossible to design a power engine. People of high intelligence, too. I doubt if the learned Commissioners —
At this point, one of the Commissioners leaned toward the Advocate. His words were not heard but the hissing of the voice carried a certain asperity.
The Advocate flushed and interrupted Seldon.
Q: We are not here to listen to speeches, Dr Seldon. Let us assume that you have made your point. Let me suggest to you that your predictions of disaster might be intended to destroy public confidence in the Imperial Government for purposes of your own.
A: That is not so.
Q: Let me suggest that you intend to claim that a period of time preceding the so-called ruin of Trantor will be filled with unrest of various types.
A: That is correct.
Q: And that by the mere prediction thereof, you hope to bring it about, and to have then an army of a hundred thousand available. 
A: In the first place, that is not so. And if it were, investigation will show you that barely ten thousand are men of military age, and none of these has training in arms.
Q: Are you acting as an agent for another?
A:  I am not in the pay of any man, Mr Advocate.
Q: You are entirely disinterested? You are serving science?
A: I am.
Q: Then let us see how. Can the future be changed, Dr Seldon?
A: Obviously. This courtroom may explode in the next few hours, or it may not. If it did, the future would undoubtedly be changed in some minor respects.
Q: You quibble, Dr Seldon. Can the overall history of the human race be changed?
A: Yes.
Q: Easily?
A: No. With great difficulty.
A: The psychohistoric trend of a planet-full of people contains a huge inertia. To be changed it must be met with something possessing a similar inertia. Either as many people must be concerned, or if the number of people be relatively small, enormous time for change must be allowed. Do you understand?
Q: I think I do. Trantor need not be ruined, if a great many people decide to act so that it will not.
A: That is right. 
🔥 
Q: As many as a hundred thousand people?
A: No, sir. That is far too few.
Q: You are sure?
A; Consider that Trantor has a population of over forty billions. Consider further that the trend leading to ruin does not belong to Trantor alone but to the Empire as a whole and the Empire contains nearly a quintillion human beings.
Q: I see. Then perhaps a hundred thousand people can change the trend, if they and their descendants labor for five hundred years.
A: I'm afraid not. Five hundred years is too short a time.
Q: Ah! In that case, Dr Seldon, we are left with this deduction to be made from your statements. You have gathered one hundred thousand people within the confines of your project. These are insufficient to change the history of Trantor within five hundred years. In other words, they cannot prevent the destruction of Trantor no matter what they do.
A: You are unfortunately correct.
Q: And on the other hand, your hundred thousand are intended for no illegal purpose.
A: Exactly.

quote.author: tslaming
quote.name: Ming
quote.text:
STRONG SIGNAL 🚨 Terafab is moving forward at lightning speed because the engineers themselves have the authority to make decisions 🔥

According to Korea’s The Elec, a Korean supplier executive said that even questions sent during the early morning hours in the US get answered within 30 minutes to an hour. In his view, working with Terafab is completely different from dealing with conventional semiconductor customers.

An executive at an overseas equipment maker went even further: “I’ve never seen this level of execution speed in the semiconductor industry.”

Building a fab involves countless questions like these, across every tool and material that goes into it. When each one gets a fast answer, the time saved keeps compounding, and that could add up to a serious head start before a single wafer is even processed.

The chip industry spent decades perfecting how a fab should run. Terafab is being built by engineers who answer a supplier’s question before the US is even awake and are trusted to decide on the spot, and that may turn out to be the most disruptive process change of all.

quote.author: levie
quote.name: Aaron Levie
quote.text:
It’s almost incomprehensible how wide the distance is between someone who’s working at the frontier with AI and basically everyone else right now. 

The crazy thing is these lines are not converging, but only growing farther apart. If the curve of AI progress had leveled off, it would certainly have given most people and companies time to catch up or implement their workflows in a standardized way. The technology would have neutralized competitive advantage because everyone would be using it the same way.

But what’s happened is the opposite. The curve of AI progress is basically going vertical right now, which means if you had codified your processes 3-6 months ago you’re likely already behind again. Now imagine most companies that kicked into gear a year ago and thought that they were done. Even further behind now.

I’ve never seen a technology in my life and career that improves at this rate, which consequently means you need to upgrade your expectations at a similar rate. Our brains weren’t wired for this, and our organizational change management processes certainly weren’t either.

With any form of recursive self improvement, things just get wilder. It’s a time when you will need to be constantly reevaluating the things that didn’t work just a couple months ago to see if they now can be solved. AI native companies certainly have a strong advantage due to this right now, so now it comes down to can the bigger companies keep up. Wild times.

Keynote ⚡ Why I'm long $TSLA & $SPCX 

Last week, I was invited to Los Angeles for the LD Micro conference to give a keynote about my two biggest investment positions Tesla and SpaceX.

Many of you follow me for my tech stock/VC investing ... but before all of that, I had a previous life as a micro-cap investor. Yup, I loved finding the tiniest companies at the earliest stages. We're talking back in high school. 2008-2011.

But in 2012, my mentor told me about his test-ride in a Tesla Roadster. This is what let me to @Tesla & realized that despite trading for $3B... the upside potential was MASSIVE. 

They were trying to change everything about our transportation and energy systems. No more fossil fuels, via super fast sports cars. I got hooked, and the more research I did, the more I invested in $TSLA. I went all in. This wasn't a car company. It was a technology company.

No innovation like this was happening in public microcap stocks. Frankly, most of them were scam businesses built to dilute shareholders, not build world changing technologies.

So naturally, I became more and more enthralled by tech companies changing the world, and eventually even startups (and now my VC has invested $40M into them!). In short, I left the microcap world and never looked back.

At one point, Chris Lahiji, a great friend and mentor, said Gali, come back to LD Micro, pitch us on Tesla & why you left microcap. So I did. That was 8 years ago, and the stock is up ~20X.

This year, Chris invited me back to reflect on Tesla's progress and offer my newest investment pick; SpaceX.

So that resulted in this talk lol. A high level overview of my investing philosophy and why my two biggest positions are Tesla & SpaceX STILL. Despite being up 20X+ on both, I think they can each 10X from here. Presented at a conference for microcap stocks lol ... two $1T+ picks 😂😂

I had a blast doing this and was honored to be invited back 🙏

quote.name: DogeDesigner
quote.text:
BREAKING: Neuralink has added a new blog update on its website. It details a 72-hour sprint to help people with ALS speak, make calls and use Grok with their thoughts.

Engineers worked at a VOICE trial participant’s home, building and testing improvements alongside him.

🧠 SPEECH AND AI

• Automatic speech detection: Recognizes when users try to speak, reducing button presses.
• Live brain activity: Shows which imagined speaking patterns produce stronger signals.
• Grok agent prototype: Think “Hey Neuralink” followed by a task, and Grok carries it out on a computer.

📱 BLOOM MOBILE APP

• Everyday use: Tested outside the lab, including ordering coffee.
• iPhone keyboard: Write in any app using speech decoded from brain signals.
• Faster editing: Easier corrections and keyboard suggestions.
• Lock-screen controls: Start speech without unlocking the phone.
• Phone calls: Send generated speech directly into calls, with an optional greeting explaining the assistive device.

🤝 BUILT WITH THE PARTICIPANT

• He, his wife and caregiver helped shape improvements.
• Direct feedback shortened development cycles from weeks to hours.
• He and his wife joked together on the phone again.

🧠 CONTINUING DEVELOPMENT

• Some demos include improvements made after the sprint.
• Neuralink is recruiting engineers.
• Devices remain investigational.

Neuralink is changing lives ♥️

posts.text:
Before Hollywood, I was living in a van in Hawaii and waiting tables at Bubba Gump Shrimp Company. One day, the incredible Rae Dawn Chong walked into the restaurant, and naturally, I went up to her table and said, “Hey, you’re a movie star! What are you doing here?”

She asked if I could act, and I said, “Fuck yeah, put me in your movie!”

She asked for my phone number. The only problem was I didn’t have one. So I gave her my buddy Mike’s number instead. A couple days later, Mike casually mentions, “Oh, by the way, someone called you.” ARE YOU KIDDING ME, MIKE?!

I called her back, and sure enough, she was serious. I drove over to pick up the script, went back to Mike’s house, and read all 120 pages three times in a row. First script I’d ever read. My character's name was Devon, and I remember thinking, “Sweet! I could totally play a Devon!”

I showed up to the audition with every line and inflection mapped out in pencil. Rae told me I could act and offered me the part. I asked if we were shooting in Hawaii. Nope. Los Angeles.

I had about $60 to my name, a bag of clothes, and some rollerblades.

Then Rae told me they'd fly me out. And I remember thinking right then and there, my life just changed forever. I'm going to be an actor.

That little movie was Cursed Part 3, a low-budget horror comedy that opened the door to Hollywood for me.

I'll forever be grateful to Rae for taking a chance on a kid working at a shrimp restaurant. Everybody starts somewhere, and this is where it all began for me.
